1175081634.whyB: The Lala-Razzies might all be non-Bloops, so even 'some' isn't forced.
1175081634.whyC: The Lala-Razzies might include Bloops, so 'none' isn't forced either.
1175081634.explanationTl: Yung Razzies na Lalas ay puwedeng may Bloops o wala. Walang pilit na conclusion, kaya cannot determine.
1175081634.stepsTl:
1. Nasa loob ng Razzies ang Bloops.
2. May Razzies na Lalas, pero puwedeng nasa labas ng Bloops.
3. Puwedeng mag-overlap o hindi ang Bloops at Lalas.
4. Cannot determine.
1175081634.hintTl: Mag-drawing ng circles: kaya mo bang i-drawing na nagtatagpo ang Bloops at Lalas, at hindi rin?

1384668205.steps:
1. Some celestial bodies are stars.
2. All stars shine, so those celestial bodies shine.
3. Some celestial bodies shine.
1384668205.hint: Follow only the members you know are in both groups.
1384668205.whyA: Only some celestial bodies are stars; the rest are unknown.
1384668205.whyC: The celestial bodies that are stars must shine, so 'none' is false.
1384668205.whyD: A conclusion does follow: at least the overlapping members.
1384668205.explanationTl: Yung celestial bodies na stars ay siguradong shine. Kaya some celestial bodies shine.
1384668205.stepsTl:
1. May celestial bodies na stars.
2. Lahat ng stars ay shine, kaya shine din ang mga iyon.
3. Some celestial bodies shine.
1384668205.hintTl: Sundan lang ang members na sigurado kang nasa parehong group.

1401712706.steps:
1. Some furniture are chairs.
2. All chairs have legs, so those furniture have legs.
3. Some furniture have legs.
1401712706.hint: Follow only the members you know are in both groups.
1401712706.whyA: Only some furniture are chairs; the rest are unknown.
1401712706.whyC: The furniture that are chairs must have legs, so 'none' is false.
1401712706.whyD: A conclusion does follow: at least the overlapping members.
1401712706.explanationTl: Yung furniture na chairs ay siguradong have legs. Kaya some furniture have legs.
1401712706.stepsTl:
1. May furniture na chairs.
2. Lahat ng chairs ay have legs, kaya have legs din ang mga iyon.
3. Some furniture have legs.
1401712706.hintTl: Sundan lang ang members na sigurado kang nasa parehong group.

1493632564.text: All teachers are educators. No educator is careless. So no teacher is careless. Is the argument valid or invalid?
1493632564.optionA: Invalid, because some teachers are careless in real life
1493632564.optionD: Invalid, because a premise with 'No' cannot give a conclusion
1493632564.explanation: Every teacher is an educator, and no educator is careless, so no teacher can be careless. The conclusion is forced: valid.
1493632564.steps:
1. Teachers sit entirely inside educators.
2. Educators and careless people never overlap.
3. So teachers and careless people never overlap.
4. Valid.
1493632564.hint: Judge only whether the conclusion is forced by the premises. Real-life truth doesn't matter.
1493632564.whyA: Validity ignores real life; accept the premises as given.
1493632564.whyB: The conclusion is forced, since teachers are fully inside a group with no careless members.
1493632564.whyD: One negative premise is allowed; only two negative premises give no conclusion.
1493632564.explanationTl: Lahat ng teacher ay educator, at walang educator na careless. Kaya walang teacher na careless. Valid.
1493632564.stepsTl:
1. Nasa loob ng educators ang teachers.
2. Walang educator na careless.
3. Kaya walang teacher na careless.
4. Valid.
1493632564.hintTl: Tingnan lang kung pilit na sumusunod ang conclusion sa premises. Hindi mahalaga kung totoo ito sa totoong buhay.

1632913086.text: If all rivers flow and no lake is a river, then:
1632913086.explanation: The premises say only that lakes are outside the rivers. Things outside the rivers may or may not flow, so nothing about lakes flowing is forced.
1632913086.steps:
1. Rivers sit inside the group 'things that flow'.
2. Lakes are outside the rivers.
3. Lakes could be inside or outside 'things that flow'.
4. Cannot determine.
1632913086.hint: Being outside a group says nothing about a bigger group that contains it.
1632913086.whyA: Not being a river doesn't make lakes flow.
1632913086.whyB: Other things besides rivers may flow; the premises don't rule lakes out.
1632913086.whyC: Even 'some' isn't forced; lakes could be completely outside the flowing things.
1632913086.explanationTl: Sinasabi lang na hindi river ang lake. Puwedeng mag-flow o hindi ang hindi-river, kaya cannot determine.
1632913086.stepsTl:
1. Nasa loob ng 'things that flow' ang rivers.
2. Nasa labas ng rivers ang lakes.
3. Puwedeng nasa loob o labas ng 'things that flow' ang lakes.
4. Cannot determine.
1632913086.hintTl: Kapag nasa labas ka ng isang group, wala itong sinasabi tungkol sa mas malaking group na naglalaman nito.

1636377641.optionA: Yes, because all actors are wealthy
1636377641.optionB: Yes, because Ben must be an actor
1636377641.optionC: No, because Ben may be wealthy without being an actor
1636377641.optionD: Yes, because only confident people are wealthy
1636377641.explanation: Being wealthy doesn't make Ben an actor, and only actors are known to be confident. So 'Ben is confident' is not undoubtedly true.
1636377641.steps:
1. Actor -> confident, and actor -> wealthy.
2. Ben is wealthy, but wealthy does not lead back to actor.
3. Without 'Ben is an actor', nothing says Ben is confident.
4. Not undoubtedly true.
1636377641.hint: Check whether 'wealthy' leads back to 'actor', or only the other way.
1636377641.whyA: All actors are wealthy, but not all wealthy people are actors.
1636377641.whyB: Reversing 'all actors are wealthy' is the classic error.
1636377641.whyD: The premise says only confident people are actors, not that only confident people are wealthy.
1636377641.explanationTl: Hindi porke wealthy si Ben ay actor na siya. Kaya hindi sigurado na confident siya.
1636377641.stepsTl:
1. Actor -> confident, at actor -> wealthy.
2. Wealthy si Ben, pero hindi bumabalik ang wealthy sa actor.
3. Kung hindi alam na actor si Ben, walang sinasabing confident siya.
4. Hindi sigurado.
1636377641.hintTl: Tingnan kung ang 'wealthy' ay bumabalik sa 'actor', o one-way lang.

1910565425.text: All birds fly. Penguins do not fly. So penguins are not birds. Is the argument valid or invalid?
1910565425.optionB: Invalid, because real penguins are birds
1910565425.optionC: Invalid, because a negative premise gives no conclusion
1910565425.explanation: If every bird flies and penguins don't fly, penguins cannot be birds. The first premise is false in real life, but validity only asks whether the conclusion follows, so the argument is valid.
1910565425.steps:
1. Birds sit entirely inside 'things that fly'.
2. Penguins are outside 'things that fly'.
3. So penguins are outside 'birds'.
4. Valid (even though premise 1 is false in real life).
1910565425.hint: Judge only whether the conclusion is forced by the premises. Real-life truth doesn't matter.
1910565425.whyB: Real-life facts don't decide validity; accept the premises as given.
1910565425.whyC: One negative premise is allowed; only two negative premises give no conclusion.
1910565425.whyD: The conclusion is forced by the premises, so it is not invalid.
1910565425.explanationTl: Kung lahat ng bird ay lumilipad at hindi lumilipad ang penguin, hindi siya bird. Mali ang premise sa totoong buhay, pero valid pa rin ang argument.
1910565425.stepsTl:
1. Nasa loob ng 'things that fly' lahat ng birds.
2. Nasa labas ng 'things that fly' ang penguins.
3. Kaya nasa labas sila ng 'birds'.
4. Valid (kahit mali ang premise 1 sa totoong buhay).
1910565425.hintTl: Tingnan lang kung pilit na sumusunod ang conclusion sa premises. Hindi mahalaga kung totoo ito sa totoong buhay.

2065221890.text: All architects design. No engineer is an architect. So no engineer designs. Is the argument valid or invalid?
2065221890.optionB: Valid, because architects and engineers are different jobs
2065221890.optionC: Valid, because the conclusion uses 'No' like the second premise
2065221890.explanation: Engineers are outside the architects, but people other than architects can still design. The conclusion is not forced, so the argument is invalid.
2065221890.steps:
1. Architects sit inside 'people who design'.
2. Engineers are outside the architects.
3. Engineers could still be inside 'people who design'.
4. The conclusion is not forced. Invalid.
2065221890.hint: Judge only whether the conclusion is forced by the premises. Real-life truth doesn't matter.
2065221890.whyA: Not being an architect doesn't stop someone from designing.
2065221890.whyB: Different jobs can share the same activity; that doesn't force the conclusion.
2065221890.whyC: Copying the 'No' of a premise is a pattern-matching trap, not logic.
2065221890.explanationTl: Hindi architect ang engineers, pero puwede pa rin silang mag-design. Hindi pilit ang conclusion, kaya invalid.
2065221890.stepsTl:
1. Nasa loob ng 'people who design' ang architects.
2. Nasa labas ng architects ang engineers.
3. Puwede pa ring mag-design ang engineers.
4. Hindi pilit. Invalid.
2065221890.hintTl: Tingnan lang kung pilit na sumusunod ang conclusion sa premises. Hindi mahalaga kung totoo ito sa totoong buhay.

2120519826.text: No pilot is afraid of heights. Some people are pilots. So some people are not afraid of heights. Is the argument valid or invalid?
2120519826.optionA: Invalid, because not all people are pilots
2120519826.optionC: Invalid, because a negative premise gives no conclusion
2120519826.optionD: Invalid, because the conclusion should be 'No people are afraid of heights'
2120519826.explanation: The people who are pilots are not afraid of heights, so at least some people are not afraid of heights. The conclusion is forced: valid.
2120519826.steps:
1. Some people are pilots.
2. No pilot is afraid of heights, so those people are not afraid.
3. Some people are not afraid of heights. Valid.
2120519826.hint: Judge only whether the conclusion is forced by the premises. Real-life truth doesn't matter.
2120519826.whyA: The conclusion only says 'some' people, so it doesn't need all people to be pilots.
2120519826.whyC: One negative premise is allowed; only two negative premises give no conclusion.
2120519826.whyD: Only some people are pilots, so 'No people' would overreach.
2120519826.explanationTl: Yung mga taong pilot ay hindi takot sa heights. Kaya may mga taong hindi takot sa heights. Valid.
2120519826.stepsTl:
1. May mga taong pilot.
2. Walang pilot na takot sa heights, kaya hindi takot ang mga iyon.
3. May mga taong hindi takot sa heights. Valid.
2120519826.hintTl: Tingnan lang kung pilit na sumusunod ang conclusion sa premises. Hindi mahalaga kung totoo ito sa totoong buhay.

910327409.explanation: Fork, spoon and knife are cutlery (eating utensils). A plate is dishware that holds the food.
910327409.hint: Find the group that three of the items share, then spot the one that doesn't belong.
910327409.whyA: Fork is cutlery like spoon and knife.
910327409.whyB: Spoon is cutlery like fork and knife.
910327409.whyC: Knife cuts, but it is still cutlery like fork and spoon.
910327409.explanationTl: Cutlery ang fork, spoon at knife. Ang plate ay lalagyan ng pagkain.
910327409.hintTl: Hanapin ang group na pareho ng tatlo, tapos hanapin ang hindi kasama.

1136389625.text: Odd one out: Guitar, Violin, Flute, Cello
1136389625.explanation: Guitar, violin and cello are string instruments. The flute is a wind instrument.
1136389625.hint: Think about how each instrument makes its sound.
1136389625.whyA: Guitar is a string instrument like violin and cello.
1136389625.whyB: Violin is a string instrument like guitar and cello.
1136389625.whyD: Cello is bowed like the violin; it is still a string instrument.
1136389625.explanationTl: String instruments ang guitar, violin at cello. Ang flute ay wind instrument, hinihipan.
1136389625.hintTl: Isipin kung paano lumalabas ang tunog ng bawat instrument.

1174300165.hint: Find the group that three of the items share, then spot the one that doesn't belong.
1174300165.whyA: Rose is a flower like tulip and daisy.
1174300165.whyB: Tulip is a flower like rose and daisy.
1174300165.whyC: Daisy is a flower like rose and tulip.
1174300165.explanationTl: Puno ang oak; flowers naman ang iba.
1174300165.hintTl: Hanapin ang group na pareho ng tatlo, tapos hanapin ang hindi kasama.

1209780052.hint: Ask what each item does on paper.
1209780052.whyA: Pen makes marks, like pencil and marker.
1209780052.whyB: Pencil makes marks, like pen and marker.
1209780052.whyC: Marker makes marks, like pen and pencil.
1209780052.explanationTl: Ang eraser ay nagbubura; ang iba ay gumagawa ng sulat o marka.
1209780052.hintTl: Tanungin kung ano ang ginagawa ng bawat isa sa papel.

1694141845.hint: Find the group that three of the items share, then spot the one that doesn't belong.
1694141845.whyA: Book is reading material like magazine and newspaper.
1694141845.whyB: Magazine is reading material like book and newspaper.
1694141845.whyC: Newspaper is reading material like book and magazine.
1694141845.explanationTl: Pansulat ang pen; babasahin naman ang iba.
1694141845.hintTl: Hanapin ang group na pareho ng tatlo, tapos hanapin ang hindi kasama.

1910354685.hint: Think about the animal class each one belongs to.
1910354685.whyA: Dog is a mammal like cat and horse.
1910354685.whyB: Cat is a mammal like dog and horse.
1910354685.whyC: Horse is a mammal like dog and cat, even if it isn't a house pet.
1910354685.explanationTl: Mammals ang dog, cat at horse. Ang bird ay hindi mammal.
1910354685.hintTl: Isipin kung anong animal class kabilang ang bawat isa.

2093024008.text: Odd one out: Apple, Banana, Carrot, Orange
2093024008.hint: Find the group that three of the items share, then spot the one that doesn't belong.
2093024008.whyA: Apple is a fruit like banana and orange.
2093024008.whyB: Banana is a fruit like apple and orange.
2093024008.whyD: Orange is a fruit like apple and banana.
2093024008.explanationTl: Gulay ang carrot; prutas naman ang iba.
2093024008.hintTl: Hanapin ang group na pareho ng tatlo, tapos hanapin ang hindi kasama.

93725730.whyA: 42 adds 8 again; the gap grows by 1 each time.
93725730.explanationTl: Ang differences ay 7, 8, 9, kaya +10 ang susunod: 34 + 10 = 44.

458469050.explanation: The differences are 4, 5, 6, so the next is 7: 18 + 7 = 25.
458469050.steps:
1. Gaps: 7-3 = 4, 12-7 = 5, 18-12 = 6.
2. The gap grows by 1, so the next gap is 7.
3. 18 + 7 = 25.
458469050.hint: Write the difference between neighbouring numbers. If it isn't constant, look at how the differences change.
458469050.whyA: 24 adds 6 again; the gap grows by 1 each time.
458469050.explanationTl: Ang differences ay 4, 5, 6, kaya +7 ang susunod: 18 + 7 = 25.
458469050.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 4, 5, 6.
2. Lumalaki ng 1, kaya +7 ang susunod.
3. 18 + 7 = 25.
458469050.hintTl: Isulat ang difference ng magkatabing numbers. Kung hindi pare-pareho, tingnan kung paano nagbabago ang differences.

1623350365.steps:
1. Gaps: 13-6 = 7, 21-13 = 8, 30-21 = 9.
2. The gap grows by 1, so the next gap is 10.
3. 30 + 10 = 40.
1623350365.hint: Write the difference between neighbouring numbers. If it isn't constant, look at how the differences change.
1623350365.whyA: 38 adds 8, a smaller gap than the last one.
1623350365.whyB: 39 adds 9 again; the gap grows by 1 each time.
1623350365.explanationTl: Ang differences ay 7, 8, 9, kaya +10 ang susunod: 30 + 10 = 40.
1623350365.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 7, 8, 9.
2. Lumalaki ng 1, kaya +10 ang susunod.
3. 30 + 10 = 40.
1623350365.hintTl: Isulat ang difference ng magkatabing numbers. Kung hindi pare-pareho, tingnan kung paano nagbabago ang differences.

2036881895.whyA: 34 adds 8 again; the gap grows by 1 each time.
2036881895.explanationTl: Ang differences ay 6, 7, 8, kaya +9 ang susunod: 26 + 9 = 35.

259095705.explanation: Article VI, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the Senate is composed of 24 senators elected at large by the qualified voters of the Philippines.
259095705.hint: Think of the number of senatorial slots on a full ballot, which is twice the number elected every three years.
259095705.whyA: 21 is not in the Constitution; it may come from confusing the count with the number of members of other bodies.
259095705.whyB: 22 is a guess just under the real figure; the Constitution fixes it at 24.
259095705.whyC: 23 is one short; the Senate has 24 seats, 12 elected every three years.
259095705.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 2 ng 1987 Constitution, 24 senators ang bumubuo sa Senate, at elected at large sila ng mga botante sa buong Pilipinas.
259095705.hintTl: Isipin mo kung ilan ang senador na binoboto every three years, tapos i-double mo.

731025093.explanation: Article XIV, Section 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino, which shall be further developed and enriched on the basis of existing Philippine and other languages.
731025093.hint: The 1987 Constitution uses a name that is not tied to any single regional language.
731025093.whyA: English is an official language for communication and instruction (Art XIV Sec 7), not the national language.
731025093.whyC: Tagalog is a regional language that Filipino is largely based on, but the Constitution names Filipino, not Tagalog.
731025093.whyD: Cebuano is a major regional language, not the national language.
731025093.explanationTl: Ayon sa Article XIV, Section 6 ng 1987 Constitution, Filipino ang national language natin. Hindi Tagalog, kahit malaki ang base nito sa Tagalog.
731025093.hintTl: Yung pangalan na ginamit ng Constitution ay hindi pangalan ng isang rehiyon lang.

1628749749.explanation: Article VI, Section 23(1) of the 1987 Constitution provides that Congress, by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, has the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war.
1628749749.hint: Declaring war is a grave act, so it needs a supermajority, the same fraction used to override a presidential veto.
1628749749.whyB: One-half (a simple majority) is too low for an act as grave as declaring war.
1628749749.whyC: Three-quarters is not used here; it is higher than what Section 23 requires.
1628749749.whyD: Three-fifths is not the fraction in Section 23; the Constitution requires two-thirds.
1628749749.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 23(1), kailangan ng two-thirds vote ng both Houses, in joint session pero voting separately, para mag-declare ng state of war ang Congress.
1628749749.hintTl: Mabigat na desisyon ang pag-declare ng war, kaya supermajority ang kailangan. Pareho ito sa fraction para ma-override ang veto ng President.

1686675808.text: Under the 1987 Constitution, how long is the term of office of a senator?
1686675808.explanation: Article VI, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the term of office of senators is six years, and no senator may serve more than two consecutive terms.
1686675808.hint: A senator's term is twice as long as the term of a member of the House of Representatives.
1686675808.whyA: 3 years is the term of a member of the House of Representatives (Art VI Sec 7), not a senator.
1686675808.whyB: 4 years is not a term used for senators under the 1987 Constitution.
1686675808.whyC: 5 years is not a constitutional term for senators; it may be confused with other fixed terms.
1686675808.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 4, six years ang term ng senador, at hanggang two consecutive terms lang ang pwede.
1686675808.hintTl: Doble ang term ng senador kumpara sa congressman.

1842092208.explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art VI), executive power in the President (Art VII), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art VIII).
1842092208.hint: Think of separation of powers: one branch makes laws, one carries them out, one interprets them.
1842092208.whyA: These are institutions, not branches; the Senate is part of Congress, so the legislature is counted twice.
1842092208.whyB: These are forms of government, not branches of government.
1842092208.whyD: The Senate is part of the Legislature, and the executive branch is missing entirely.
1842092208.explanationTl: Separation of powers: Legislative (Congress, Art VI), Executive (President, Art VII), at Judicial (Supreme Court at lower courts, Art VIII).
1842092208.hintTl: Isa ang gumagawa ng batas, isa ang nagpapatupad, at isa ang nag-i-interpret.

1137112436.text: Under Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution, the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a ____ ecology.
1137112436.explanation: Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution states that the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.
1137112436.hint: The phrase pairs the idea of nature in equilibrium with the idea of human health.
1137112436.whyB: 'Clean and green' is a popular campaign slogan, not the constitutional wording.
1137112436.whyC: 'Safe and sanitary' sounds like health-code language, not Article II, Section 16.
1137112436.whyD: 'Productive and sustainable' echoes development policy terms, not the exact constitutional phrase.
1137112436.explanationTl: Sa Article II, Section 16, ang right ng tao ay sa isang 'balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.'
1137112436.hintTl: Dalawang idea ang pinagsama: balanse ng kalikasan at kalusugan ng tao.

1276088687.text: Which of the following is one of the norms of conduct of public officials and employees under Section 4 of RA 6713?
1276088687.explanation: Section 4(A) of RA 6713 lists eight norms of conduct: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living. Professionalism is Section 4(A)(b).
1276088687.hint: Recall the norm about performing duties with excellence, intelligence and skill.
1276088687.whyB: RA 6713 requires the opposite, political neutrality: services are provided without partisanship.
1276088687.whyC: Seniority is a factor in some personnel actions, but it is not one of the eight norms in Section 4.
1276088687.whyD: The norms call for commitment to public interest above personal interest, not personal loyalty to superiors.
1276088687.explanationTl: Sa Section 4(A) ng RA 6713, walo ang norms of conduct, at isa dito ang professionalism: dapat excellent, competent at skilled ang pagganap sa trabaho.
1276088687.hintTl: Alalahanin mo yung norm tungkol sa pagtatrabaho nang may excellence at skill.

176394152.explanation: Nitrogen's chemical symbol is N, a single capital letter, because the element name begins with N and no other element took that letter.
176394152.hint: Some elements use just the first letter of their name.
176394152.explanationTl: N ang symbol ng nitrogen. Isang letter lang, yung first letter ng pangalan niya.
176394152.hintTl: May mga element na first letter lang ng pangalan ang symbol.

951529665.hint: He was a Scottish scientist who noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish.
951529665.whyB: Marie Curie is known for research on radioactivity (radium and polonium).
951529665.whyC: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization and early vaccines, not penicillin.
951529665.whyD: Jonas Salk developed the polio vaccine.
951529665.explanationTl: Si Alexander Fleming ang naka-discover ng penicillin noong 1928, at ito ang naging simula ng modern antibiotics.
951529665.hintTl: Scottish scientist siya na nakapansin na pinapatay ng amag ang bacteria sa petri dish.

1404617270.text: Which inert gas is most commonly used to fill incandescent light bulbs to prevent the filament from oxidizing?
1404617270.explanation: Argon is the gas most commonly used to fill incandescent bulbs because it is inert, cheap and plentiful (about 1% of air), so it keeps the hot tungsten filament from reacting with oxygen.
1404617270.hint: It is the most abundant noble gas in Earth's air.
1404617270.whyA: Helium is inert but conducts heat away too fast and is not the usual bulb fill.
1404617270.whyC: Neon is known for glowing signs, not for filling ordinary incandescent bulbs.
1404617270.whyD: Hydrogen is not inert; it is flammable and is not used as a bulb fill.
1404617270.explanationTl: Argon ang karaniwang nilalagay sa incandescent bulb kasi inert ito, mura at marami sa hangin (mga 1%), kaya hindi nag-o-oxidize ang filament.
1404617270.hintTl: Ito ang pinakamaraming noble gas sa hangin natin.

1497615111.hint: The two lightest elements are also the two most abundant in the universe.
1497615111.whyA: Hydrogen is the MOST abundant element, not the second.
1497615111.whyC: Oxygen is the third most abundant in the universe and the most abundant in Earth's crust.
1497615111.whyD: Carbon is common in living things but far less abundant than helium in the universe.
1497615111.explanationTl: Helium ang second most abundant element sa universe, kasunod ng hydrogen na number one.
1497615111.hintTl: Yung dalawang pinakamagaang element ay sila ring pinakamarami sa universe.

1734316344.hint: This river flows entirely within China and passes the Three Gorges Dam.
1734316344.whyB: The Yellow River (Huang He) is China's second-longest river, shorter than the Yangtze.
1734316344.whyC: The Mekong is long (about 4,900 km) but shorter than the Yangtze.
1734316344.whyD: The Ganges is about 2,500 km, far shorter than the Yangtze.
1734316344.explanationTl: Ang Yangtze River sa China ang pinakamahabang ilog sa Asia, mga 6,300 km.
1734316344.hintTl: Nasa China lang ito at dito makikita ang Three Gorges Dam.

1785343423.explanation: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand.
1785343423.hint: It is the city where the Grand Palace stands.
1785343423.whyB: Chiang Mai is a major city in northern Thailand, not the capital.
1785343423.whyC: Phuket is a resort island in southern Thailand.
1785343423.whyD: Pattaya is a beach resort city, not the capital.
1785343423.explanationTl: Bangkok ang capital ng Thailand at ito rin ang pinakamalaking city nila.

1822712201.hint: He received the first U.S. patent for the telephone in 1876.
1822712201.whyA: Thomas Edison is known for the phonograph and a practical light bulb, not the telephone.
1822712201.whyC: Nikola Tesla is known for alternating current (AC) systems.
1822712201.whyD: Guglielmo Marconi is known for radio (wireless telegraphy).
1822712201.explanationTl: Si Alexander Graham Bell ang kinikilalang imbentor ng telephone; nakuha niya ang patent noong 1876.
1822712201.hintTl: Siya ang nakakuha ng unang U.S. patent para sa telephone noong 1876.

1996658139.hint: Its symbol is written with a Y and two bars (the same sign is used by China's currency).
1996658139.whyA: The yuan is the currency of China.
1996658139.whyC: The won is the currency of South Korea (and North Korea).
1996658139.whyD: The ringgit is the currency of Malaysia.
1996658139.hintTl: Y na may dalawang guhit ang symbol nito.

2132758750.hint: The capital is a planned city built because two rival big cities could not agree which should be capital.
2132758750.whyA: Sydney is Australia's largest city, not its capital.
2132758750.whyB: Melbourne was the temporary seat of government (1901-1927) but is not the capital.
2132758750.whyD: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland state, not of Australia.
2132758750.explanationTl: Canberra ang capital ng Australia. Planned city ito na pinili bilang compromise sa pagitan ng Sydney at Melbourne.
2132758750.hintTl: Hindi ito yung pinakamalaking city; ginawa ito bilang compromise ng dalawang malaking city.

113688723.explanation: The United States recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946 through the Treaty of Manila; June 12, 1898 was the declaration of independence from Spain.
113688723.hint: It happened the year after World War II ended.
113688723.whyB: 1898 is when independence from Spain was declared in Kawit, Cavite, not when the U.S. granted independence.
113688723.whyC: 1935 is when the Commonwealth was inaugurated, a transition period before independence.
113688723.whyD: 1965 has no link to independence; it is the year Ferdinand Marcos was first elected president.
113688723.explanationTl: Noong July 4, 1946, kinilala ng United States ang independence ng Pilipinas sa Treaty of Manila. Yung 1898 naman ay declaration of independence mula sa Spain.
113688723.hintTl: Nangyari ito isang taon pagkatapos ng World War II.

416474926.text: Boracay Island, famous for its white sand beaches, is part of which province?
416474926.explanation: Boracay Island belongs to the municipality of Malay in the province of Aklan, Western Visayas, off the northwest tip of Panay.
416474926.hint: It is the Panay province also known for the Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo.
416474926.whyB: Antique is a neighbouring Panay province on the west coast, but Boracay is not part of it.
416474926.whyC: Capiz is another Panay province, known as the seafood capital, not Boracay's province.
416474926.whyD: Palawan is famous for El Nido and Coron beaches, not Boracay.
416474926.explanationTl: Ang Boracay ay nasa bayan ng Malay, sa probinsya ng Aklan, Western Visayas, sa northwest tip ng Panay.
416474926.hintTl: Ito yung probinsya sa Panay na sikat din sa Ati-Atihan festival sa Kalibo.

982838073.explanation: The sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) was proclaimed the national flower in 1934 by Governor-General Frank Murphy; it symbolizes purity and simplicity.
982838073.hint: Its small white blooms are strung into garlands sold outside churches.
982838073.whyA: Orchids such as the waling-waling are prized Philippine flowers, but the official national flower is the sampaguita.
982838073.whyC: The rose is not native and has no official status in the Philippines.
982838073.whyD: The sunflower has no official status in the Philippines.
982838073.explanationTl: Sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) ang national flower natin, idineklara noong 1934 ni Governor-General Frank Murphy. Simbolo ito ng purity at simplicity.
982838073.hintTl: Yung maliit na puting bulaklak na ginagawang kwintas at binebenta sa labas ng simbahan.

1503912089.explanation: Baguio is called the 'City of Pines' because of its cool highland climate and the Benguet pine trees that cover its hills.
1503912089.hint: It is the cool mountain city that also serves as the Summer Capital of the Philippines.
1503912089.whyA: Davao is known as the home of the durian and Mount Apo, not pine forests.
1503912089.whyC: Cebu is known as the 'Queen City of the South'.
1503912089.whyD: Manila is the national capital, a lowland city without pine forests.
1503912089.explanationTl: Baguio ang 'City of Pines' dahil malamig doon at puno ng pine trees ang mga bundok.
1503912089.hintTl: Ito rin ang tinatawag na Summer Capital ng Pilipinas.

2022609578.text: Siargao Island, known as the 'Surfing Capital of the Philippines', is part of which province?
2022609578.explanation: Siargao Island, home of the Cloud 9 surf break, is part of the province of Surigao del Norte in the Caraga Region.
2022609578.hint: Its province shares the 'Surigao' name and lies at the northern tip of Mindanao.
2022609578.whyA: Surigao del Sur is a neighbouring province on the east coast of Mindanao, but Siargao is not part of it.
2022609578.whyB: Dinagat Islands is a separate island province in Caraga, north of Siargao, not Siargao's province.
2022609578.whyD: Agusan del Norte is a Caraga province on the Mindanao mainland, not Siargao's province.
2022609578.explanationTl: Ang Siargao, kung saan nandoon ang Cloud 9 surf break, ay part ng Surigao del Norte sa Caraga Region.
2022609578.hintTl: Ang probinsya nito ay may 'Surigao' sa pangalan at nasa northern tip ng Mindanao.

1226545578.steps:
1. Subtract 4 from both sides: x = 12 − 4.
2. So x = 8.
3. Check: 8 + 4 = 12 ✓
1226545578.hint: Move the 4 to the other side by doing the opposite operation.
1226545578.explanationTl: Ibawas ang 4 sa magkabilang side, kaya x = 12 − 4 = 8.
1226545578.stepsTl:
1. Ibawas ang 4 sa magkabilang side: x = 12 − 4.
2. Kaya x = 8.
3. I-check: 8 + 4 = 12 ✓
1226545578.hintTl: Ilipat ang 4 sa kabilang side gamit ang opposite operation.

476202559.whyB: 5/7 comes from adding the tops (2 + 3) and the bottoms (3 + 4) instead of multiplying.
476202559.whyC: 1/3 is not the product; 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12, which simplifies to 1/2.
476202559.whyD: 5/12 adds the numerators (2 + 3) but multiplies the denominators; both must be multiplied.
476202559.hintTl: Sa multiplication ng fractions, top × top at bottom × bottom, tapos i-simplify.

1629422152.steps:
1. The denominators are already the same (5).
2. Add the numerators: 1 + 3 = 4.
3. Keep the denominator: 4/5.
1629422152.whyC: 1/5 is just the first fraction; you still need to add the 3/5.
1629422152.explanationTl: Pareho na ang denominator, kaya i-add lang ang numerators: 1 + 3 = 4, so 4/5.
1629422152.stepsTl:
1. Pareho na ang denominator (5).
2. I-add ang numerators: 1 + 3 = 4.
3. Sagot: 4/5.

1810348430.explanation: Same denominators, so add the numerators: 1/6 + 5/6 = 6/6 = 1.
1810348430.steps:
1. The denominators are already the same (6).
2. Add the numerators: 1 + 5 = 6, giving 6/6.
3. Simplify: 6/6 = 1.
1810348430.whyD: 3/6 comes from adding the denominators too (6/12); only the numerators are added.
1810348430.explanationTl: Pareho ang denominator, kaya i-add lang ang numerators: 6/6, na katumbas ng 1.
1810348430.stepsTl:
1. Pareho na ang denominator (6).
2. I-add ang numerators: 1 + 5 = 6, kaya 6/6.
3. I-simplify: 6/6 = 1.

1569990510.text: A rectangular lot is 10 m long and 5 m wide. What is its area?
1569990510.explanation: Area of a rectangle = length × width = 10 m × 5 m = 50 sq m.
1569990510.steps:
1. Area = length × width.
2. 10 × 5 = 50.
3. Area = 50 sq m.
1569990510.hint: Area covers the inside of the shape, not the distance around it.
1569990510.whyB: 30 is the perimeter: 2 × (10 + 5). Area multiplies length by width.
1569990510.whyC: 15 just adds length and width; area multiplies them.
1569990510.whyD: 100 squares the length (10 × 10) and ignores the width.
1569990510.explanationTl: Ang area ng rectangle ay length × width: 10 × 5 = 50 sq m.
1569990510.stepsTl:
1. Area = length × width.
2. 10 × 5 = 50.
3. Area = 50 sq m.
1569990510.hintTl: Ang area ay ang loob ng shape, hindi ang ikot sa paligid.

2118687031.text: What is the sum of the interior angles of a decagon (10-sided polygon)?
2118687031.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°. For n = 10: 8 × 180° = 1,440°.
2118687031.hint: A polygon with n sides can be split into (n − 2) triangles.
2118687031.whyB: 1,800° uses n × 180°; you must subtract 2 from the number of sides first.
2118687031.whyC: 1,260° is (9 − 2) × 180°, the angle sum of a 9-sided polygon.
2118687031.explanationTl: Ang sum ng interior angles ay (n − 2) × 180°. Sa decagon, n = 10, kaya 8 × 180° = 1,440°.
2118687031.hintTl: Ang polygon na may n sides ay mahahati sa (n − 2) na triangles.

20506394.steps:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time.
2. 25 km ÷ 0.5 h = 50.
3. Speed = 50 km/h.
20506394.whyB: 40 km/h would cover only 20 km in half an hour.
20506394.whyC: 60 km/h would cover 30 km in half an hour, not 25 km.
20506394.whyD: 30 km/h would cover only 15 km in half an hour.
20506394.explanationTl: Speed = distance ÷ time. 25 km ÷ 0.5 h = 50 km/h; parang dinoble lang kasi kalahating oras.
20506394.stepsTl:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time.
2. 25 km ÷ 0.5 h = 50.
3. Speed = 50 km/h.

36851876.whyA: 30 adds 5 again; the gaps grow by 2 each time (next gap is 11).
36851876.whyC: 42 is not a perfect square; the terms are 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so next is 6².
36851876.explanationTl: Squares ang pattern: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², kaya ang susunod ay 6² = 36.

188829606.steps:
1. Each term is the sum of the two before it: 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5, 3 + 5 = 8, 5 + 8 = 13.
2. Next: 8 + 13 = 21.
188829606.hint: Compare each term with the two terms just before it.
188829606.whyB: 18 adds 5 (the gap before last); the rule adds the previous two terms.
188829606.whyC: 16 doubles 8; the rule is to add the last two terms, 8 + 13.
188829606.explanationTl: Bawat term ay sum ng dalawang nauna. Kaya 8 + 13 = 21.
188829606.stepsTl:
1. Bawat term = sum ng dalawang nauna: 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5, 3 + 5 = 8, 5 + 8 = 13.
2. Susunod: 8 + 13 = 21.
188829606.hintTl: Ikumpara ang bawat term sa dalawang term bago nito.

195237896.whyB: 24 adds 8 (the last gap); the terms are multiplied by 2, not increased by a fixed amount.
195237896.whyD: 28 adds 12; each term is doubled, so 16 × 2 = 32.

414065780.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 1, 8, 27, 64, ?
414065780.explanation: The terms are cubes: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, so the next is 5³ = 125.
414065780.hint: Check whether each term is a whole number raised to the same power.
414065780.whyA: 100 is 10² (a square); the terms are cubes.
414065780.whyD: 81 is 9², which fits a squares pattern, not 1, 8, 27, 64.
414065780.explanationTl: Cubes ang pattern: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, kaya ang susunod ay 5³ = 125.
414065780.hintTl: Tingnan kung ang bawat term ay number na naka-power ng pareho.

1596450503.text: What is the range of the data set 10, 20, 30, 40?
1596450503.hint: Range measures the spread from the smallest to the largest value.
1596450503.whyB: 25 is the mean, not the range.
1596450503.whyC: 40 is only the highest value; subtract the lowest value from it.
1596450503.whyD: 20 is a single value from the list; range = highest − lowest.
1596450503.hintTl: Ang range ay ang layo ng pinakamaliit at pinakamalaking value.

221276860.text: A wire frame is shaped like a cube with edges 3 cm long. How much wire is used for all the edges?
221276860.explanation: A cube has 12 edges, so the total length is 12 × 3 cm = 36 cm.
221276860.steps:
1. A cube has 12 edges.
2. Each edge is 3 cm.
3. Total wire = 12 × 3 = 36 cm.
221276860.hint: Count the edges: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom, and 4 vertical ones.
221276860.whyA: 24 cm uses 8 (the number of corners) instead of 12 edges.
221276860.whyB: 18 cm uses 6 (the number of faces) instead of 12 edges.
221276860.whyD: 27 is the volume (3 × 3 × 3) in cubic cm, not the total edge length.
221276860.explanationTl: May 12 edges ang cube, kaya 12 × 3 cm = 36 cm ng wire.
221276860.stepsTl:
1. May 12 edges ang cube.
2. Bawat edge ay 3 cm.
3. Total = 12 × 3 = 36 cm.
221276860.hintTl: Bilangin ang edges: 4 sa taas, 4 sa baba, at 4 na patayo.

635433018.text: A backyard has chickens and goats. There are 20 heads and 56 legs in all. How many goats are there?
635433018.explanation: If all 20 were chickens there would be 40 legs; the extra 16 legs come from goats at 2 extra legs each, so 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
635433018.steps:
1. Let c = chickens, g = goats: c + g = 20 and 2c + 4g = 56.
2. If all 20 were chickens: 20 × 2 = 40 legs.
3. Extra legs: 56 − 40 = 16.
4. Each goat adds 2 extra legs: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
5. Check: 12 chickens × 2 + 8 goats × 4 = 24 + 32 = 56 ✓
635433018.hint: Pretend every animal is a chicken, then see how many legs are left over.
635433018.whyA: 12 is the number of chickens, not goats.
635433018.whyB: 6 goats would give 14 chickens and 28 + 24 = 52 legs, not 56.
635433018.whyC: 10 goats would give 10 chickens and 20 + 40 = 60 legs, not 56.
635433018.explanationTl: Kung lahat manok, 40 legs lang. Ang sobrang 16 legs ay galing sa kambing, tig-2 extra bawat isa, kaya 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
635433018.stepsTl:
1. c + g = 20 at 2c + 4g = 56.
2. Kung lahat manok: 20 × 2 = 40 legs.
3. Sobra: 56 − 40 = 16.
4. Bawat kambing may 2 extra legs: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
5. Check: 12 × 2 + 8 × 4 = 24 + 32 = 56 ✓
635433018.hintTl: Isipin munang lahat ay manok, tapos tingnan kung ilang legs ang sobra.

1640625305.text: Ana saves ₱1,500 every month. How much will she have saved after 2 years?
1640625305.hint: Convert the years into months first.
1640625305.whyA: ₱18,000 is the savings for only 1 year (12 months).

33274110.whyB: 14 doubles the time, but the extra tailors cancel out the extra suits.
33274110.whyC: 3.5 halves the time for the extra tailors but forgets there are twice as many suits.
33274110.whyD: 10 has no basis; each tailor makes 1 suit in 7 days, so 14 tailors make 14 suits in 7 days.
33274110.explanationTl: Isang tailor = 1 suit sa 7 days. Kaya 14 tailors = 14 suits sa 7 days din.

372469145.text: Pedro can paint a room in 6 hours, and Jose can paint the same room in 3 hours. Working together, how many hours will they take?
372469145.explanation: Pedro paints 1/6 of the room per hour and Jose 1/3; together 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 per hour, so 2 hours.
372469145.steps:
1. Pedro's rate: 1/6 room per hour.
2. Jose's rate: 1/3 room per hour.
3. Together: 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 room per hour.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2 hours.
372469145.hint: Add their rates (part of the job per hour), not their times.
372469145.whyA: 4.5 is the average of 6 and 3; working together is faster than either one alone.
372469145.whyB: 9 adds the two times; together they should finish faster, not slower.
372469145.whyD: 3 is Jose's time alone; Pedro's help makes it shorter.
372469145.explanationTl: Si Pedro 1/6 ng room kada oras, si Jose 1/3. Sabay: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 kada oras, kaya 2 hours.
372469145.stepsTl:
1. Pedro: 1/6 kada oras.
2. Jose: 1/3 kada oras.
3. Sabay: 1/6 + 2/6 = 1/2 kada oras.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2 hours.
372469145.hintTl: I-add ang rates nila (bahagi ng trabaho kada oras), hindi ang oras.

472237019.text: 6 workers can finish a road repair in 10 days. Working at the same rate, how many days will 15 workers take?
472237019.steps:
1. Total work = 6 workers × 10 days = 60 worker-days.
2. With 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.
472237019.hint: More workers means fewer days: find the total worker-days first.
472237019.whyA: 25 treats it as a direct proportion (10 × 15 ÷ 6); more workers should mean fewer days.
472237019.whyC: 6 is the original number of workers, not the new number of days.
472237019.whyD: 5 just halves the days; 15 workers is 2.5 times as many, so days are divided by 2.5.
472237019.explanationTl: Ang trabaho ay 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. Hatiin sa 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.
472237019.stepsTl:
1. Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days.
2. Sa 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.
472237019.hintTl: Mas maraming workers, mas kaunting araw. Hanapin muna ang total worker-days.

1621855505.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 4 hours, while a drain can empty it in 12 hours. If both are open, how many hours will it take to fill the empty tank?
1621855505.explanation: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12 = 3/12 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6 tank per hour, so it takes 6 hours.
1621855505.steps:
1. Pipe fills 1/4 tank per hour.
2. Drain empties 1/12 tank per hour.
3. Net: 3/12 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6 tank per hour.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/6 = 6 hours.
1621855505.hint: The drain works against the pipe, so subtract its rate.
1621855505.whyA: 3 adds the two rates (1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3); the drain takes water out, so subtract.
1621855505.whyB: 8 subtracts the times (12 − 4); subtract the rates instead.
1621855505.whyC: 16 adds the times (4 + 12); work problems combine rates, not times.
1621855505.explanationTl: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12 = 1/6 ng tank kada oras, kaya 6 hours bago mapuno.
1621855505.stepsTl:
1. Pipe: 1/4 tank kada oras.
2. Drain: 1/12 tank kada oras (bawas).
3. Net: 3/12 − 1/12 = 1/6 kada oras.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/6 = 6 hours.
1621855505.hintTl: Kontra ang drain sa pipe, kaya i-subtract ang rate nito.

1689327113.whyB: 4 halves the time because there are half as many chefs, but there are also half as many dishes.
1689327113.whyC: 16 doubles the time for fewer chefs but forgets there are fewer dishes too.
1689327113.whyD: 12 has no basis; each chef cooks 1 dish in 8 minutes, so 4 chefs cook 4 dishes in 8 minutes.
1689327113.explanationTl: Isang chef = 1 dish sa 8 minutes. Kaya 4 chefs = 4 dishes sa 8 minutes din.

14256358.hint: Which kind of speech would make people listen closely and not want it to end?
14256358.whyA: Monotonous means dull and in one flat tone; it would bore an audience, not captivate it.
14256358.whyC: Vague means unclear; an unclear speech loses listeners instead of holding them.
14256358.whyD: Abrupt means sudden or curt; it describes how a speech ends or its tone, not why it captivates.
14256358.explanationTl: Ang 'eloquent' ay magaling at malinaw magsalita, kaya na-captivate ang audience. Yung ibang choices (monotonous, vague, abrupt) ay negative, kaya hindi sila tugma sa 'captivated'.
14256358.hintTl: Anong klaseng speech ang gugustuhin mong pakinggan hanggang dulo?

637573758.text: Fill in the blank: The horse jumped _____ the fence without touching it.
637573758.explanation: 'Over' shows movement from one side of something to the other, passing above it. 'Without touching it' rules out 'on', which means landing on the fence's surface.
637573758.hint: The horse never touched the fence. Which preposition means passing above something to the other side?
637573758.whyA: 'On' means landing on the surface of the fence, which contradicts 'without touching it'.
637573758.whyC: 'In' means inside something; you cannot jump inside a fence.
637573758.whyD: 'At' shows direction toward a target (jumped at someone), not clearing an obstacle.
637573758.explanationTl: Ang 'over' ay paglampas sa ibabaw papunta sa kabilang side. Dahil sabi 'without touching it', hindi pwede ang 'on' kasi ibig sabihin nun lumapag siya sa fence.
637573758.hintTl: Hindi tinamaan ng kabayo ang fence. Anong preposition ang ibig sabihin ay lumampas sa ibabaw?

800041561.hint: 'News' ends in -s, but is it really plural?
800041561.whyA: 'The' is the correct article here; nothing is wrong with it.
800041561.whyB: 'News' is the correct noun; the problem is the verb that agrees with it.
800041561.whyD: 'Good' is a correct predicate adjective after a linking verb.
800041561.explanationTl: Kahit may -s sa dulo, ang 'news' ay singular (uncountable noun). Kaya dapat 'The news is good', hindi 'are'.
800041561.hintTl: May -s ang 'news', pero plural ba talaga siya?

838470859.hint: Ownership with 'belong' always uses the same preposition: belong ___ someone.
838470859.whyB: 'Belong with' means fitting in a group or place (that cup belongs with the set), not ownership.
838470859.whyC: 'For' is a common Filipino-English slip; 'belong for' is not standard English.
838470859.whyD: 'Of' shows possession in phrases like 'the book of John', but 'belong' does not take 'of'.
838470859.explanationTl: Ang tamang idiom ay 'belong to' kapag pagmamay-ari. 'The book belongs to her' = kanya ang libro.
838470859.hintTl: Pag ownership, laging 'belong ___ someone'. Anong preposition yun?

904422609.text: Identify the error: 'Each of the players play well.'
904422609.explanation: The subject is 'Each', which is always singular; 'of the players' is only a prepositional phrase. The verb must be 'plays'.
904422609.hint: Find the real subject first. Is it 'Each' or 'players'?
904422609.whyA: 'Each' is correct; it is the singular subject the verb must agree with.
904422609.whyB: 'Players' is correctly plural inside the phrase 'of the players'; it is not the subject.
904422609.whyD: 'Well' is the correct adverb for the verb 'play'; 'good' would be the mistake.
904422609.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'Each', at laging singular yan. Yung 'of the players' ay prepositional phrase lang, hindi siya ang subject. Kaya dapat 'Each of the players plays well.'
904422609.hintTl: Hanapin muna ang totoong subject. 'Each' ba o 'players'?

986518591.hint: Some nouns name one object but are always plural, like 'pants' and 'eyeglasses'.
986518591.whyA: 'The' is the correct article; nothing is wrong with it.
986518591.whyB: 'Scissors' is the correct form; 'scissor' as a noun for the tool is not standard.
986518591.explanationTl: Ang 'scissors' ay laging plural, tulad ng 'pants' at 'eyeglasses'. Kaya dapat 'The scissors are sharp.'
986518591.hintTl: May mga noun na isang bagay lang pero laging plural, tulad ng 'pants'.

1106854031.hint: Look for the helping verb that points to something that has not happened yet.
1106854031.whyA: 'She eats' is simple present, for habits or general facts.
1106854031.whyB: 'She ate' is simple past; the action is already done.
1106854031.whyD: 'She is eating' is present progressive, an action happening right now.
1106854031.explanationTl: Ang 'will + base verb' ay simple future tense. Ang 'will eat' ay kakain pa lang siya.
1106854031.hintTl: Hanapin ang helping verb na nagsasabing mangyayari pa lang.

1365006955.text: Identify the error: 'Every member of the jury have voted.'
1365006955.explanation: The subject is 'member', made singular by 'Every'; 'of the jury' is only a prepositional phrase. The verb must be 'has voted'.
1365006955.hint: What is the head noun of the subject, and is it singular or plural?
1365006955.whyA: 'Every' is correct; it is what makes the subject singular.
1365006955.whyB: 'Member' is correctly singular after 'Every'; 'members' would be wrong.
1365006955.whyD: 'Voted' is the correct past participle; only the helping verb is wrong.
1365006955.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'member', at singular siya dahil sa 'Every'. Yung 'of the jury' ay phrase lang. Kaya dapat 'Every member of the jury has voted.'
1365006955.hintTl: Ano ang main noun ng subject? Singular ba o plural?

1444166743.hint: Ignore 'of the decision'. What is the real subject?
1444166743.whyA: 'Were' is plural; the subject 'impact' is singular.
1444166743.whyC: 'Are' is plural and also present tense; the subject 'impact' is singular.
1444166743.whyD: 'Have significant' is ungrammatical; 'significant' is an adjective and needs a linking verb like 'was'.
1444166743.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'impact' (singular), hindi 'decision'. Kaya singular verb: 'The impact of the decision was significant.'
1444166743.hintTl: Huwag pansinin ang 'of the decision'. Ano ang totoong subject?

1562931377.hint: Ignore 'of the experiment'. Is the real subject singular or plural?
1562931377.whyA: 'Was' agrees with 'experiment', the noun closest to the blank, but the subject is 'results'.
1562931377.whyC: 'Is' is singular; the subject 'results' is plural.
1562931377.whyD: 'Has surprising' is ungrammatical; an adjective needs a linking verb, and 'has' is singular anyway.
1562931377.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'results' (plural), hindi 'experiment'. Kaya plural verb: 'The results of the experiment were surprising.'
1562931377.hintTl: Huwag pansinin ang 'of the experiment'. Singular ba o plural ang totoong subject?

1142168602.explanation: A basic English sentence follows article + noun (subject), then the linking verb, then the adjective: 'The flowers are beautiful.'
1142168602.hint: Start with the subject (article + noun), then the verb.
1142168602.whyA: It puts the adjective 'beautiful' in the subject slot and the noun after the verb, so the sentence makes no sense.
1142168602.whyC: The verb 'are' splits the article 'The' from its noun 'flowers'.
1142168602.whyD: The article 'the' must come before its noun, not after it.
1142168602.explanationTl: Ang basic na ayos: article + noun (subject), tapos verb, tapos adjective. Kaya 'The flowers are beautiful.'
1142168602.hintTl: Unahin ang subject (article + noun), saka ang verb.

1691343255.explanation: The subject 'the cat' comes first, then the progressive verb 'is sleeping' (helping verb + present participle): 'The cat is sleeping.'
1691343255.hint: Keep the article with its noun, and keep 'is' right before 'sleeping'.
1691343255.whyA: It puts 'sleeping' in the subject slot and leaves 'cat' at the end with no role.
1691343255.whyC: The verb 'is' splits the article 'The' from its noun 'cat'.
1691343255.whyD: The article 'the' must come before its noun, not after it.
1691343255.explanationTl: Una ang subject na 'the cat', tapos ang verb na 'is sleeping' (helping verb + -ing). Kaya 'The cat is sleeping.'
1691343255.hintTl: Dapat magkasama ang article at noun, at 'is' bago ang 'sleeping'.

1965033272.text: What is implied by the sentence 'The movie was exciting, but the ending was predictable.'?
1965033272.optionB: The ending was less exciting than the rest of the movie.
1965033272.explanation: 'But' sets up a contrast: the movie overall was exciting, while the ending, being predictable, did not keep up that excitement.
1965033272.hint: What does the word 'but' contrast the ending with?
1965033272.whyA: Too strong: the sentence calls the movie exciting, so it does not say the movie was bad.
1965033272.whyC: Contradicts the sentence: a predictable ending is the opposite of a surprising one.
1965033272.whyD: Overgeneralizes: only the ending is called predictable; the rest was exciting.
1965033272.explanationTl: Ang 'but' ay nagpapakita ng contrast: exciting ang movie, pero predictable ang ending, kaya hindi kasing-exciting ang ending kumpara sa iba.
1965033272.hintTl: Ano ang kinokontra ng 'but' sa ending?

83162521.hint: A businessman described this way would be hard to fool.
83162521.whyA: Foolish is the opposite of astute.
83162521.whyC: Naive means inexperienced and easily fooled, the opposite of astute.
83162521.whyD: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, the opposite of astute.
83162521.explanationTl: Ang 'astute' ay matalino at magaling bumasa ng sitwasyon, parang 'shrewd' o wais. Ang ibang choices ay kabaligtaran.
83162521.hintTl: Ang ganitong businessman ay mahirap lokohin.

200646296.hint: Think of a long climb up a steep mountain.
200646296.whyA: Easy is the opposite of arduous.
200646296.whyC: Simple is the opposite of arduous.
200646296.whyD: Effortless is the opposite of arduous, which means needing great effort.
200646296.explanationTl: Ang 'arduous' ay mahirap at nakakapagod, kailangan ng matinding effort. Kaya 'difficult' ang sagot.
200646296.hintTl: Isipin ang pag-akyat sa matarik na bundok.

1464501749.hint: How would you feel facing this task before you even start?
1464501749.whyA: Easy is the opposite; a daunting task looks hard.
1464501749.whyC: Simple is the opposite; a daunting task looks complicated.
1464501749.whyD: Straightforward is the opposite; a daunting task looks overwhelming.
1464501749.explanationTl: Ang 'daunting' ay nakakatakot o nakakapanghina ng loob dahil mukhang mahirap. Kaya 'intimidating' ang sagot.
1464501749.hintTl: Ano ang pakiramdam mo bago mo pa simulan ang ganitong task?

1697800269.text:
The scientist examined the minute details of the cell.

In this sentence, 'minute' most nearly means:
1697800269.explanation: As an adjective (pronounced my-NOOT), 'minute' means extremely small; details of a cell are tiny. The time-unit meaning (MIN-it) is a noun and does not fit here.
1697800269.hint: Here 'minute' describes details. How big are the details of a single cell?
1697800269.whyB: That is the noun 'minute' (60 seconds); in this sentence the word is an adjective describing 'details'.
1697800269.whyC: Confuses 'minute' with doing something 'in a minute' (quickly); the word describes size, not speed.
1697800269.whyD: Details can be important, but 'minute' describes their size, not their importance.
1697800269.explanationTl: Dito, adjective ang 'minute' (basa: my-NOOT) at ang ibig sabihin ay napakaliit. Ang 'minute' na 60 seconds ay noun, kaya hindi bagay dito.
1697800269.hintTl: Inilalarawan ng 'minute' ang details. Gaano kalaki ang details ng isang cell?

35942117.text: Broom is to sweeping as needle is to:
35942117.explanation: A broom is the tool used for sweeping; a needle is the tool used for sewing. The pair is tool : the job it does.
35942117.hint: Ask: what job is this tool made to do?
35942117.whyB: Ironing uses a flat iron, not a needle.
35942117.whyC: Weaving is done on a loom by interlacing threads, not with a sewing needle.
35942117.whyD: Folding is done by hand; it is not a needle's job.
35942117.explanationTl: Ang broom ay ginagamit sa sweeping, at ang needle naman ay ginagamit sa sewing. Tool : ang ginagawa nito ang relationship.
35942117.hintTl: Tanungin mo: ano ang trabaho ng tool na 'to?

183168070.hint: Think of the main action each tool performs.
183168070.whyB: Nailing is the hammer's job, not the saw's.
183168070.whyC: Sanding is done with sandpaper or a sander.
183168070.whyD: Drilling is done with a drill.
183168070.explanationTl: Ang hammer ay pang-pound, ang saw naman ay pang-cut. Tool : action ang pattern.
183168070.hintTl: Isipin mo kung ano ang main na ginagawa ng bawat tool.

327417457.hint: Pair each quantity with its standard unit.
327417457.whyD: Newtons measure force (including weight), not mass.
327417457.explanationTl: Ang area ay sinusukat in square meters, at ang mass ay in kilograms. Quantity : unit ang relationship.
327417457.hintTl: I-match mo ang bawat quantity sa standard unit nito.

571070274.hint: Which option is a unit of time?
571070274.explanationTl: Ang angle ay sinusukat in degrees, ang time naman in seconds. Quantity : unit ulit ang pattern.
571070274.hintTl: Alin sa options ang unit ng time?

828334311.explanation: An odometer is the instrument that shows mileage; a compass is the instrument that shows direction. The pair is instrument : what it indicates.
828334311.hint: What reading does each instrument give you?
828334311.whyA: Speed is shown by a speedometer, not a compass.
828334311.whyB: Hiking is an activity where a compass may be used, not what it indicates.
828334311.whyC: The needle is a part of the compass, not what it indicates.
828334311.explanationTl: Ang odometer ay nagpapakita ng mileage, ang compass naman ay nagpapakita ng direction. Instrument : ang sinusukat nito.
828334311.hintTl: Anong reading ang binibigay ng bawat instrument?

1555712605.hint: What is a camera's basic job, the way measuring is a ruler's?
1555712605.whyB: Printing is done by a printer after the photo is taken, not by the camera.
1555712605.whyC: Lighting comes from a flash or lamp; it is not the camera's main purpose.
1555712605.whyD: Focusing is one step in using a camera, not what it is for.
1555712605.explanationTl: Ang ruler ay pang-measure, ang camera naman ay pang-photograph. Tool : main purpose nito.
1555712605.hintTl: Ano ang basic na trabaho ng camera, gaya ng pag-measure sa ruler?

1631256051.hint: Find the unit used for length or distance.
1631256051.explanationTl: Ang volume ay in liters, ang distance naman in meters. Quantity : unit.
1631256051.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang unit ng length o distance.

1707578260.hint: Recall the SI unit for the flow of electric charge.
1707578260.whyA: Volts measure voltage (potential difference), not current.
1707578260.explanationTl: Ang length ay in meters, ang electric current naman in amperes. Huwag malito sa volts (voltage), ohms (resistance) at watts (power).
1707578260.hintTl: Alalahanin mo ang SI unit ng electric current.

269705685.text: Statement: "To win the inter-school debate, our team must prepare its arguments early." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
269705685.optionA: Preparing early guarantees that the team will win.
269705685.optionB: The team wants to win the inter-school debate.
269705685.optionC: The other teams have not prepared at all.
269705685.optionD: Debates are judged only on how early teams prepare.
269705685.explanation: The speaker is planning how to win, so the statement takes for granted that the team wants to win. The other options claim more than the statement says.
269705685.hint: An assumption is something the speaker takes for granted; watch out for words like 'guarantees' and 'only'.
269705685.whyA: 'Must prepare' means preparing is needed, not that it guarantees a win.
269705685.whyC: The statement says nothing about the other teams.
269705685.whyD: 'Only' goes too far; early preparation can matter without being the sole basis of judging.
269705685.explanationTl: Nagpaplano ang speaker kung paano mananalo, kaya assumed na gusto talagang manalo ng team. Yung ibang options, sobra na sa sinasabi ng statement.
269705685.hintTl: Ang assumption ay yung tinatanggap na lang ng speaker na totoo; ingat sa mga salitang 'guarantees' at 'only'.

796708615.text: Statement: "To raise office morale, the new division chief plans to personally thank employees for good work." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
796708615.optionA: Being thanked can lift employees' morale.
796708615.optionB: Thanking employees is the only way to raise morale.
796708615.optionC: Office morale is already at its highest.
796708615.optionD: Employees care only about cash bonuses.
796708615.explanation: The chief would use thanks to raise morale only if thanking people can actually lift it, so that is the assumption. The other options overstate or contradict the plan.
796708615.hint: Ask: what must the chief believe for this plan to make sense?
796708615.whyB: 'Only way' overstates it; the plan needs thanks to help, not to be the sole method.
796708615.whyC: If morale were already at its highest, there would be no need to raise it, so this contradicts the statement.
796708615.whyD: If employees cared only about bonuses, thanking them would not work, so this goes against the plan.
796708615.explanationTl: Gagamitin lang ng chief ang pag-thank para tumaas ang morale kung naniniwala siyang nakakataas talaga ito ng morale. Yun ang assumption.
796708615.hintTl: Tanungin mo: ano ang dapat paniwalaan ng chief para may sense ang plan niya?

823971108.text: Statement: "Maria enrolled in a review center so that she can pass the Civil Service Exam." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
823971108.optionA: Maria has failed the Civil Service Exam before.
823971108.optionB: Review centers guarantee that every enrollee passes.
823971108.optionC: Studying on one's own never works.
823971108.optionD: A review center can help her prepare for the exam.
823971108.explanation: Maria enrolls in order to pass, so she must believe the review center can help her prepare. The other options are not needed for her decision to make sense.
823971108.hint: Look for the belief behind Maria's reason for enrolling, not an extreme claim.
823971108.whyA: The statement does not say whether she has taken the exam before.
823971108.whyB: 'Guarantee that every enrollee passes' is too strong; she only needs the review to help.
823971108.whyC: 'Never works' is too strong; she can choose a review center without believing self-study is useless.
823971108.explanationTl: Nag-enroll si Maria para pumasa, kaya naniniwala siya na makakatulong ang review center sa pag-prepare niya. Yun ang assumption.
823971108.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang paniniwala sa likod ng dahilan ni Maria, hindi yung extreme na claim.

985585971.text: Statement: "The company requires its new call-center agents to practise speaking English for one hour every day." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
985585971.optionA: The new agents already speak perfect English.
985585971.optionB: Every agent will become fluent within one month.
985585971.optionC: Daily speaking practice can improve the agents' English.
985585971.optionD: The agents will never need any other language at work.
985585971.explanation: The company requires the practice because it believes practice can improve the agents' English. The other options are either contradicted by the rule or not needed for it.
985585971.hint: Why would the company bother requiring the practice?
985585971.whyA: If they already spoke perfect English, the practice would be pointless, so this contradicts the rule.
985585971.whyB: The rule expects improvement, not a specific result within one month.
985585971.whyD: 'Never' goes too far; the rule only needs English to matter, not to be the only language used.
985585971.explanationTl: Nire-require ng company ang practice kasi naniniwala silang gagaling ang English ng agents dahil dito. Yun ang assumption.
985585971.hintTl: Bakit pa ire-require ng company ang practice?

105547188.explanation: Each number is coded as the square of the next number, (n + 1)^2, so 6 = 7^2 = 49.
105547188.hint: Look at the right-hand numbers: are they perfect squares?
105547188.explanationTl: Ang bawat number ay naging square ng kasunod na number, (n + 1)^2, kaya 6 = 7^2 = 49.
105547188.hintTl: Tingnan mo ang numbers sa kanan: perfect squares ba sila?
105547188.whyA: 48 is 7^2 - 1; it misses the perfect-square pattern by one.
105547188.whyC: 50 adds 14 to 36; the jumps are 9, 11, 13, so the next jump is 13, not 14.
105547188.whyD: 51 adds 15 to 36, skipping a step in the jumps 9, 11, 13.

587274041.steps:
1. Differences: 18 - 10 = 8, 28 - 18 = 10; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 12, so 28 + 12 = 40.
3. Check with n^2 + 3n: 5^2 + 3(5) = 25 + 15 = 40.
587274041.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
587274041.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 18 - 10 = 8, 28 - 18 = 10; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 12, kaya 28 + 12 = 40.
3. I-check: 5^2 + 3(5) = 25 + 15 = 40.
587274041.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
587274041.whyA: 38 adds 10 again; the differences grow by 2 (8, 10, 12).
587274041.whyB: 39 is one short; usually from using n^2 + 2n + 4, which does not fit 3 = 18.
587274041.whyD: 41 overshoots by one; the next difference is 12, not 13.

1695189728.explanation: The coded values go up by 9, then 11, so the next jump is 13: 31 + 13 = 44. The rule is n^2 + 4n - 1.
1695189728.steps:
1. Differences: 20 - 11 = 9, 31 - 20 = 11; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 13, so 31 + 13 = 44.
3. Check with n^2 + 4n - 1: 25 + 20 - 1 = 44.
1695189728.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
1695189728.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ng coded values ay 9, tapos 11, kaya ang susunod ay 13: 31 + 13 = 44. Ang rule ay n^2 + 4n - 1.
1695189728.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 20 - 11 = 9, 31 - 20 = 11; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 13, kaya 31 + 13 = 44.
3. I-check: 25 + 20 - 1 = 44.
1695189728.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
1695189728.whyB: 45 assumes n^2 + 3n + 5, which gives 15 for n = 2, not 11.
1695189728.whyC: 46 adds 15; the differences go 9, 11, 13, so the next is 13.
1695189728.whyD: 47 adds 16, overshooting the +2 growth in the differences.

1966047099.hint: Try writing each coded value as a product of two consecutive numbers.
1966047099.explanationTl: Ang bawat number ay naging (n + 1)(n + 2): 3 x 4 = 12, 4 x 5 = 20, 5 x 6 = 30, kaya 5 = 6 x 7 = 42.
1966047099.hintTl: Subukan mong isulat ang bawat value bilang product ng dalawang magkasunod na numbers.
1966047099.whyB: 44 adds 14; the differences go 8, 10, 12, so the next is 12.
1966047099.whyC: 46 comes from the wrong rule n^2 + 3n + 6, which gives 16 for n = 2.
1966047099.whyD: 48 adds 18, far more than the next difference of 12.

2050284569.explanation: The coded values go up by 9, then 11, so the next jump is 13: 30 + 13 = 43. The rule is n^2 + 4n - 2.
2050284569.steps:
1. Differences: 19 - 10 = 9, 30 - 19 = 11; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 13, so 30 + 13 = 43.
3. Check with n^2 + 4n - 2: 25 + 20 - 2 = 43.
2050284569.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
2050284569.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ng coded values ay 9, tapos 11, kaya ang susunod ay 13: 30 + 13 = 43. Ang rule ay n^2 + 4n - 2.
2050284569.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 19 - 10 = 9, 30 - 19 = 11; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 13, kaya 30 + 13 = 43.
3. I-check: 25 + 20 - 2 = 43.
2050284569.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
2050284569.whyA: 42 adds 12; the differences go 9, 11, 13, so the next is 13.
2050284569.whyC: 44 comes from the rule n^2 + 3n + 4, which gives 14 for n = 2, not 10.
2050284569.whyD: 45 adds 15, overshooting the +2 growth in the differences.

2069883621.steps:
1. Differences: 11 - 5 = 6, 19 - 11 = 8; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 10, so 19 + 10 = 29.
3. Check with n^2 + 3n + 1: 16 + 12 + 1 = 29.
2069883621.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
2069883621.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 11 - 5 = 6, 19 - 11 = 8; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 10, kaya 19 + 10 = 29.
3. I-check: 16 + 12 + 1 = 29.
2069883621.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
2069883621.whyA: 28 adds 9; the differences go 6, 8, 10, so the next is 10.
2069883621.whyC: 30 adds 11, overshooting the +2 growth in the differences.
2069883621.whyD: 31 adds 12, as if the differences grew by 4.

636588524.text: A graph shows the noon temperature in a town: Monday 15 °C, Tuesday 20 °C, Wednesday 25 °C. What is the average temperature for the three days?
636588524.steps:
1. Add the values: 15 + 20 + 25 = 60.
2. Divide by the number of days: 60 / 3 = 20.
3. Average = 20 °C.
636588524.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many there are.
636588524.whyA: 18 °C is below the middle value; with evenly spaced values the average equals the middle one.
636588524.whyD: 24 °C is close to the highest reading, not the average.
636588524.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang values: 15 + 20 + 25 = 60.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng araw: 60 / 3 = 20.
3. Average = 20 °C.
636588524.hintTl: I-add mo lahat, tapos i-divide sa dami ng values.

734611293.text: A graph shows the noon temperature in a city: Day 1 25 °C, Day 2 30 °C, Day 3 35 °C. What is the average temperature for the three days?
734611293.steps:
1. Add the values: 25 + 30 + 35 = 90.
2. Divide by the number of days: 90 / 3 = 30.
3. Average = 30 °C.
734611293.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many there are.
734611293.whyA: 28 °C is below the middle value; with evenly spaced values the average equals the middle one.
734611293.whyD: 34 °C is close to the highest reading, not the average.
734611293.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang values: 25 + 30 + 35 = 90.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng araw: 90 / 3 = 30.
3. Average = 30 °C.
734611293.hintTl: I-add mo lahat, tapos i-divide sa dami ng values.

763597739.text: A graph shows a factory's rice-sack production: Q1 500 sacks, Q2 550 sacks, Q3 600 sacks. What is the average production per quarter?
763597739.steps:
1. Add the values: 500 + 550 + 600 = 1,650.
2. Divide by the number of quarters: 1,650 / 3 = 550.
3. Average = 550 sacks.
763597739.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many quarters there are.
763597739.whyA: 540 is below the middle value; with evenly spaced values the average equals the middle one.
763597739.whyD: 570 leans toward the highest quarter instead of the average.
763597739.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang values: 500 + 550 + 600 = 1,650.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng quarters: 1,650 / 3 = 550.
3. Average = 550 sacks.
763597739.hintTl: I-add mo lahat, tapos i-divide sa dami ng quarters.

1429217809.text: A graph shows a store's monthly sales: January ₱100,000, February ₱150,000, March ₱120,000. What is the average monthly sales, rounded to the nearest peso?
1429217809.hint: Add all three months, then divide by 3.
1429217809.whyB: ₱120,000 is the middle (median) value, not the average.
1429217809.whyD: ₱125,000 is the midpoint of the lowest and highest months, ignoring March's value.
1429217809.explanationTl: Average = 370,000 / 3 = ₱123,333.33, o ₱123,333 kapag ni-round sa pinakamalapit na peso.
1429217809.hintTl: I-add mo ang tatlong buwan, tapos i-divide sa 3.

413502916.explanation: P is Q's father and Q is R's mother, so P is R's grandfather and R is P's grandchild.
413502916.steps:
1. P is Q's father: P is one generation above Q.
2. Q is R's mother: Q is one generation above R.
3. So P is two generations above R: R is P's grandchild.
413502916.hint: Count the generations from P down to R.
413502916.whyB: R is Q's child, not P's child.
413502916.whyC: Siblings share the same generation; R is two generations below P.
413502916.whyD: R is below P in the family line, not above.
413502916.explanationTl: Si P ang father ni Q, at si Q ang mother ni R. Kaya grandfather ni R si P, at grandchild ni P si R.
413502916.stepsTl:
1. Si P ang father ni Q: isang generation sa taas ni Q.
2. Si Q ang mother ni R: isang generation sa taas ni R.
3. Kaya dalawang generation ang layo: grandchild ni P si R.
413502916.hintTl: Bilangin mo ang generations mula kay P pababa kay R.

505467647.explanation: Q is a daughter of both P and R. P is Q's mother, so R is Q's father, which makes R P's husband.
505467647.steps:
1. P is Q's mother.
2. Q is R's daughter, so R is Q's other parent.
3. Q's mother is P, so R is Q's father.
4. Q's father is P's husband.
505467647.hint: Q has two parents; one of them is already named as the mother.
505467647.whyA: R is Q's parent, a generation above Q, so R cannot be P's son.
505467647.whyC: Q is the daughter; R is Q's parent.
505467647.whyD: R is Q's father, not P's father.
505467647.explanationTl: Si Q ay anak ni P at ni R. Mother si P, kaya father si R, at husband siya ni P.
505467647.stepsTl:
1. Si P ang mother ni Q.
2. Si Q ay daughter ni R, kaya si R ang isa pang parent ni Q.
3. Mother na si P, kaya father si R.
4. Ang father ni Q ay husband ni P.
505467647.hintTl: Dalawa ang parents ni Q; yung isa, na-mention na bilang mother.

887372409.explanation: F is the daughter of both E and G. E is F's father, so G is F's mother, which makes G E's wife.
887372409.steps:
1. E is F's father.
2. F is G's daughter, so G is F's other parent.
3. F's father is E, so G is F's mother.
4. F's mother is E's wife.
887372409.hint: F has two parents; one of them is already named as the father.
887372409.whyA: G is F's parent, a generation above F, and must be female, so not E's son.
887372409.whyC: F is the daughter; G is F's parent.
887372409.whyD: G is F's mother, not E's mother.
887372409.explanationTl: Si F ay anak ni E at ni G. Father si E, kaya mother si G, at wife siya ni E.
887372409.stepsTl:
1. Si E ang father ni F.
2. Si F ay daughter ni G, kaya si G ang isa pang parent ni F.
3. Father na si E, kaya mother si G.
4. Ang mother ni F ay wife ni E.
887372409.hintTl: Dalawa ang parents ni F; yung isa, na-mention na bilang father.

8810366.text: No poets are lazy. Some people are poets. Which conclusion follows?
8810366.explanation: The people who are poets cannot be lazy, since no poet is lazy. So at least some people are not lazy; nothing is known about the people who are not poets.
8810366.steps:
1. No poets are lazy.
2. Some people are poets.
3. Those people, being poets, are not lazy.
4. So some people are not lazy.
8810366.hint: Focus only on the people who are poets.
8810366.whyB: We know nothing about people who are not poets, so we cannot say no one is lazy.
8810366.whyC: This contradicts the premises: some people (the poets) are not lazy.
8810366.whyD: No poets are lazy, so no lazy person can be a poet.
8810366.explanationTl: Yung mga tao na poets, hindi lazy kasi walang poet na lazy. Kaya at least some people are not lazy; wala tayong alam sa mga hindi poets.
8810366.stepsTl:
1. Walang poet na lazy.
2. May mga tao na poets.
3. Yung mga yun, dahil poets, hindi lazy.
4. Kaya some people are not lazy.
8810366.hintTl: Mag-focus ka lang sa mga tao na poets.

104501795.text: All dogs bark. Spot barks. Which conclusion follows?
104501795.optionC: It cannot be determined whether Spot is a dog.
104501795.explanation: The premise says every dog barks, not that only dogs bark. Since other animals may bark too, Spot's barking does not tell us whether Spot is a dog.
104501795.steps:
1. All dogs bark: dogs are inside the group of barkers.
2. Spot is in the group of barkers.
3. The barkers may include non-dogs.
4. So we cannot tell whether Spot is a dog.
104501795.hint: Does 'all dogs bark' also mean 'only dogs bark'?
104501795.whyA: This reverses the premise (affirming the consequent); barking does not prove Spot is a dog.
104501795.whyB: Nothing rules out Spot being a dog; dogs bark too.
104501795.whyD: 'All dogs bark' does not mean only dogs bark; this reverses the premise.
104501795.explanationTl: Sabi ng premise, lahat ng dogs ay nagba-bark, pero hindi sinabi na dogs lang ang nagba-bark. Kaya hindi natin masasabi kung dog si Spot.
104501795.stepsTl:
1. All dogs bark: kasama ang dogs sa grupo ng nagba-bark.
2. Kasama si Spot sa nagba-bark.
3. Pwedeng may hindi dog sa grupong yun.
4. Kaya cannot be determined kung dog si Spot.
104501795.hintTl: Ang 'all dogs bark' ba ay pareho ng 'only dogs bark'?

733498225.explanation: Every tree grow, and some plants are trees, so at least those plants grow. We cannot say all or none.
733498225.steps:
1. All trees grow.
2. Some plants are trees.
3. Those plants therefore grow.
4. So some plants grow.
733498225.hint: Look only at the plants that are trees.
733498225.whyA: Only some plants are trees; the others may not grow.
733498225.whyC: This contradicts the premises: the plants that are trees do grow.
733498225.whyD: A definite conclusion does follow: the overlap guarantees 'some'.
733498225.explanationTl: Lahat ng trees ay nag-grow, at may mga plants na trees, kaya at least yung mga yun ay nag-grow. Hindi natin masasabing lahat o wala.
733498225.stepsTl:
1. All trees grow.
2. Some plants are trees.
3. Kaya yung mga plants na yun ay nag-grow.
4. Kaya some plants grow.
733498225.hintTl: Tingnan mo lang yung mga plants na trees.

812446768.explanation: Every bird have feathers, and some animals are birds, so at least those animals have feathers. We cannot say all or none.
812446768.steps:
1. All birds have feathers.
2. Some animals are birds.
3. Those animals therefore have feathers.
4. So some animals have feathers.
812446768.hint: Look only at the animals that are birds.
812446768.whyA: Only some animals are birds; the others may not have feathers.
812446768.whyC: This contradicts the premises: the animals that are birds do have feathers.
812446768.whyD: A definite conclusion does follow: the overlap guarantees 'some'.
812446768.explanationTl: Lahat ng birds ay may feathers, at may mga animals na birds, kaya at least yung mga yun ay may feathers. Hindi natin masasabing lahat o wala.
812446768.stepsTl:
1. All birds have feathers.
2. Some animals are birds.
3. Kaya yung mga animals na yun ay may feathers.
4. Kaya some animals have feathers.
812446768.hintTl: Tingnan mo lang yung mga animals na birds.

1114052581.text: All dogs are loyal. No cat is a dog. Which conclusion follows?
1114052581.optionD: Nothing definite follows about whether cats are loyal.
1114052581.explanation: The premises say dogs are loyal, but they say nothing about animals that are not dogs. Cats may or may not be loyal, so no definite conclusion about cats follows.
1114052581.steps:
1. All dogs are loyal: dogs sit inside the group of loyal animals.
2. No cat is a dog: cats are outside the dog group.
3. Cats could still be inside or outside the loyal group.
4. So nothing definite follows about cats.
1114052581.hint: Being outside the dog group does not tell you whether you are outside the loyal group.
1114052581.whyA: A common error: 'not a dog' does not mean 'not loyal'; other animals can be loyal too.
1114052581.whyB: Nothing in the premises says cats are loyal.
1114052581.whyC: This might be true, but it does not follow from the premises.
1114052581.explanationTl: Sinabi lang na loyal ang dogs; walang sinabi tungkol sa hindi dogs. Kaya hindi natin alam kung loyal ang cats o hindi.
1114052581.stepsTl:
1. All dogs are loyal: nasa loob ng loyal group ang dogs.
2. No cat is a dog: nasa labas ng dog group ang cats.
3. Pwedeng nasa loob o labas ng loyal group ang cats.
4. Kaya walang definite na conclusion tungkol sa cats.
1114052581.hintTl: Ang pagiging hindi dog ay hindi nangangahulugang hindi loyal.

1862564295.explanation: Every planet have orbits, and some celestial bodies are planets, so at least those celestial bodies have orbits. We cannot say all or none.
1862564295.steps:
1. All planets have orbits.
2. Some celestial bodies are planets.
3. Those celestial bodies therefore have orbits.
4. So some celestial bodies have orbits.
